Finding: EMULATE: "האם אנחנו באמת" question-opener — shared-inquiry arc
Detail: Ynet wellness headline uses 'האם אנחנו באמת צריכים...' — rhetorical question with 'באמת' (really?) plus first-person plural 'אנחנו'. Technique: validates the reader's existing assumption before pivoting to evidence, creating a shared-inquiry tone rather than expert-to-reader instruction. The article lands at a discriminating conclusion: supplements useful for specific sub-populations, not wholesale condemned or endorsed. Apply this arc when opening Bari comparison pages — open from the familiar behavior, then pivot.

Finding: AVOID: Listicle verdict framing — 'N foods with low nutritional value' moral register
Detail: Mako article '6 מאכלים עם ערך תזונתי נמוך במיוחד' uses the 'empty calories' frame as a moral verdict on foods rather than a description of what a food provides and what it lacks. The listicle structure + 'ערך תזונתי נמוך' label slides into prescriptive moralizing. Typical tell: foods are sentenced, not described. Bari should instead name what a product provides and what it omits, then let the reader conclude. Avoid the 'empty' / 'bad' verdict form.
